name: Ronald Reagan
role: US president (1981-1989); governor of California (1967-1975); film and television actor
summary: Reagan was a movement conservative who held that government was the main obstacle to prosperity and liberty. He cut taxes and regulation, favored free trade and school choice, opposed abortion, backed school prayer and a large military, and sought to defeat Soviet communism through pressure while also negotiating arms reductions. He signed an immigration law that combined enforcement with legalization for long-resident unauthorized immigrants.

notes: Born 1911, died 2004. He was a New Deal Democrat until the 1950s and switched to the Republican Party in 1962; answers use his positions as president and in the 1964 Goldwater speech. On abortion he signed California's 1967 Therapeutic Abortion Act as governor but from about 1980 on opposed abortion firmly, and the later position is used. His 1986 immigration law is read as a record of enforcement plus legalization. Where his rhetoric (low taxes, balanced budget) differed from his record (TEFRA and other tax rises, large deficits) the answer follows the stated position and says so. Few answers rely on inference; none was added to pass the inclusion check. Later pass 2026-11-13 (rules 7): sources tagged by kind; racial-franchise, which rested only on Wikipedia, is re-sourced to his signing of the 1982 Voting Rights Act extension (act). The Gutenberg State of the Union text and the Miller Center speech set are cited or declined. All 60 Miller Center speeches and the Gutenberg State of the Union text were downloaded and searched by keyword for about 50 themes (same-sex marriage, minimum wage, deterrence, Grenada and force without the UN, nation first, the UN, school prayer, democratic peace, Lebanon, climate, term limits, the draft, English, income-tax abolition and flat tax, privatisation, unions, regulation, trade, welfare, death penalty, the ERA, balanced budget, school choice, abortion, euthanasia, nuclear power, affirmative action, line-item veto, Israel and Palestine, self-determination, South Africa, Education Department, Social Security, the Fed, immigration, guns, drugs, AIDS, civil rights). Earlier sweep of the Miller Center set by keyword for prayer in schools, nuclear power, term limits, the draft, Grenada, the United Nations, quotas and the balanced budget: new answers (expand-nuclear, end-racial-preferences from words; no-religion-state-schools and term-limits from his prayer-amendment and Moscow remarks; arm-foreign-insurgents from his 1988 Contra aid request and EO 12611, and pay-off-national-debt from Treasury/OMB debt figures as record over his words); school prayer (only silent-prayer remarks at conventions), term limits, the draft, Grenada and UN enforcement settled nothing, and same-sex marriage, minimum wage and English-as-official-language had no hits.

booksNotUsed.reason: The Voteview member matching the name is John Henninger Reagan (Texas, 1857-1891), a different person; Ronald Reagan never sat in Congress.

His principal speeches are cited from the American Presidency Project copies of the same texts (the inaugurals, the 1964 Goldwater address, State of the Union addresses, tax and immigration signings) or read by theme in the Miller Center set and not cited because they add no position beyond the answers recorded.
